text:
keisha: Quick thread  can we land a short, machine-actionable play for SI co-sell + marketplace flows? last sprint there was confusion about ownership and multiple outreach emails to the same buyer. want a small set of deterministic rules and a minimal intake payload.

omar: +1. propose we call it the "ownership arbitration flow". basic priority: 1) contract-level evidence from SI (signed SOW/PO/invoice/customer-copied email) => SI primary; 2) marketplace purchase that explicitly lists partner_id => SI primary; 3) Redwood-originated inbound (trial, in-app request) => Redwood primary; 4) concurrent documented engagement (within a short window) => shared ownership with split responsibilities.

felix: Suggest different wording for the window: "engagement assertion window" = 9 days by default. If both parties assert within that window, create a joint plan. Also add "pilot-funded precedence": if SI or partner underwrites a pilot (PO/SOW dated before engagement) they get priority even if RW originally touched lead.

renee: ops note: marketplace metadata is flaky. propose an autotag heuristic: if sku_prefix == "prt_" OR checkout.meta.partner_handle present OR order_notes include a known partner email domain -> auto-tag SI. Otherwise leave unassigned and surface to ops queue for manual assign.

ops-bot: Ticket OPS-12077 created: "marketplace autotag heuristics for partner attribution" assigned to renee, due 2024-08-01.

keisha: Love the autotag idea. Also we need a tiny intake mapping for SFDC ingestion — keep field names new to avoid collisions. Draft snippet below (copy-paste friendly):

```
lead_source_enum: [redwood, si, marketplace, hw_partner]
engagement_proof: url_or_text (required for si)
proof_kind: [sow, po, invoice, email, portal_action]
ownership_ttl_days: 9
assign_to: [redwood, si, joint]
escalation_contact: partnerships@redwood.com
lockbox_until: timestamp_or_null
```

omar: good. small addition: require at least one proof_kind==email or proof URL that includes a partner domain for automated SI assignment. If missing, mark as "needs_proof" and ping SI/SE via intake workflow.

felix: For disputes: 48 hour initial triage, if unresolved after 3 business days automatically lock assignment to the earliest documented outreach and send the buyer and both parties a short status note. call the period the "lockbox period" so legal folks see consistent language.

legal-bot: Reminder: any automatic lock language needs to be reviewed. Please submit a short clause to LR-799 by 2024-07-18. We prefer conservative wording that preserves customer experience.

renee: Ops UX: add a 4-line handoff card that appears in SFDC when assign_to != null: 1) 1-line deal summary, 2) named POCs (buyer, SI POC, RW POC), 3) procurement channel (marketplace/PO/reseller), 4) next action + ETA. This should be copyable to email/portal.

keisha: Good. Also propose two canned emails: one for assignment, one for lock. Short templates:

Assign template:
"Hi <buyer>, routing update: primary contact for this engagement is <entity>. Next step: <action> (owner: <POC>, ETA: <date>)."

Lock template:
"Hi <buyer>, ownership temporarily locked to <entity> after review. Contact for next steps: <POC>. If you think this is incorrect, reply and we'll expedite review."

omar: Action owners? I can draft the one-pager and a tiny flow diagram (Assert -> Validate -> Assign -> Notify). renee: can you wire the autotag ticket and SFDC field changes? felix: can you draft the dispute timeline + lockbox copy for legal?

felix: yes, i'll draft and ping legal-bot LR-799. aim Wed EOD.

renee: will own OPS-12077 and the SFDC ingest mapping. I'll post the tracker link here when complete.

ops-bot: OPS-12077 link: https://tracker.redwood/OPS-12077 (assigned renee).

keisha: timeline: want a publishable partner-portal blurb + SFDC changes by Friday so SEs get guidance next week. small ask: if anyone has a short anonymized customer example (where ownership ambiguity cost us the meeting), drop it here and we'll anonymize and include in FAQ.

omar: i'll add an anonymized example about an OEM deal that spanned reseller chains.

keisha: perfect. thanks team — this keeps it small and automatable. :tada:
